assessments for consideration and final determination by the board of public works including reviewing company
information returns and preparing valuation recommendations.

value among the counties in which the utility operates.
The allocation can be based on direct assignment of taxable income to a county or an allocation formula.
The taxable value of large high-cost facilities that may be located in a single county but which serve the entire
utility system are not allocated to only the county containing the facility.
The state auditor determines the taxes for each county using applicable levy rates of each county applied to the
assessed valuation allocated to each county.
Within a limited time period, a utility may appeal a valuation or petition for relief from
an erroneous assessment pursuant to West Virginia code.
A company operating large electric transmission facilities in West Virginia but having no other utility operations
in the state are evaluated the same as public utilities that have production transmission and distribution operate
operations in West Virginia. The lack of local generation or distribution operations or lack of local revenue and
income does not mean that the transmission facilities must be valued solely by netbook cost. Under the unit
method, if applicable, the state may consider the value of the integrated transmission business as a whole and
determine a portion of net operating income attributable to West Virginia and then apply the capitalization rate to that net operating income.
